title: The beginning
blurb: The Quran gives the order of these events, not their dates. The sequence is fixed; the years are unknown.

events.title: A khalifah on earth
events.what: Allah tells the angels He will place a successor on earth. They ask why, fearing bloodshed. He answers that He knows what they do not.

events.title: Adam, the first human
events.what: Allah creates Adam, teaches him the names of all things, and makes him the first prophet.

events.title: The first salam
events.what: Adam is told to greet a group of angels. He says 'As-salamu alaykum' and they reply with more. It becomes the greeting of his children.

events.title: Iblis refuses to bow
events.what: The angels bow to Adam. Iblis refuses out of pride and vows to mislead Adam's children.

events.title: Hawwa, from one soul
events.what: From Adam, Allah creates his wife so that he may find rest with her. Every person on earth descends from these two.
events.note: The Quran says only 'its mate'. The name Hawwa comes from hadith.

events.title: Sent down to earth
events.what: Adam and Hawwa eat from the forbidden tree, repent, and are sent down to earth. Allah accepts their repentance.

events.title: Am I not your Lord?
events.what: Allah draws all of Adam's descendants from his loins and asks, 'Am I not your Lord?' They all answer, 'Yes, we testify.'
events.note: A narration from Ibn Abbas, reported by Ahmad, places this at Na'man near Arafah. Scholars differ on how to read the scene.

events.title: Habil and Qabil
events.what: One son of Adam kills the other. The Quran uses it to teach that killing one person is like killing all people.

events.title: Shith, the heir of Adam
events.what: Tradition says Adam's son Shith carries on his father's guidance. Many family lines, including Nuh's, are traced through him.
events.note: Shith is not named in the Quran. His story comes from early historians, partly from Jewish sources.

events.title: Adam's death
events.what: Adam dies after a long life, surrounded by his descendants. A hadith says he once gave years of his life to Dawud, then forgot when death came: so his children forget too.
events.note: Reported by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan sahih. Versions differ on the number of years.

events.title: Prophet Idris
events.what: Prophet Idris, praised as truthful and raised to a high station. Tradition credits him with the first writing and sewing.

events.title: The first idols
events.what: Righteous men named Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr die. Their people make statues to remember them. Later generations worship the statues.

events.title: Nuh builds the ark
events.what: Nuh preaches for 950 years. His people reject him, so he builds the ark on Allah's command.

events.title: Two wives who betrayed
events.what: Nuh's own wife rejects his message. The Quran pairs her with Lut's wife: being married to a prophet saves no one who will not believe.

events.title: The Flood
events.what: The flood drowns the deniers, including Nuh's own son. The ark comes to rest on Mount Judi.

events.title: He is not of your family
events.what: Nuh pleads for his drowned son. Allah tells him the boy was not of his family, for his deeds were not righteous. Nuh asks forgiveness.

events.title: A new beginning
events.what: Nuh and the believers leave the ark in peace and blessing. Allah makes his descendants the ones who remain on earth.
events.note: Tradition names his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith as ancestors of the nations. The names come from the commentators and the Bible, not the Quran.

events.title: People reach Australia
events.what: People cross the sea from Asia to Australia. Their descendants keep one of the oldest living cultures on earth.
events.tie: The Quran says all people spread from one soul and its mate (4:1), across every land and sea.
events.note: Dates are debated, from about 65,000 to 50,000 years ago. The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: Painted caves
events.what: In caves from Indonesia to France, people paint animals and leave their hand prints. Some paintings are over 40,000 years old.
events.tie: The Quran tells people to travel the earth and see how creation began (29:20).
events.note: The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: People reach the Americas
events.what: Hunters cross from Asia into the Americas as the Ice Age ends. By 14,500 years ago they live as far south as Chile.
events.tie: The Quran says Allah made people into nations and tribes so they would know one another (49:13).
events.note: Some sites suggest people arrived thousands of years earlier. The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: Göbekli Tepe
events.what: On a hill near Urfa, people raise rings of huge carved stone pillars. It is one of the oldest known places of worship, older than farming.
events.tie: People gathered to worship before they farmed or wrote; the Quran says humans were created to worship (51:56).
events.note: What was worshipped there is unknown. The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: Farming begins
events.what: In the Fertile Crescent people sow wheat and barley and tame sheep and goats. Villages like Jericho grow into the first towns.
events.tie: The Quran asks people to look at their food: rain poured down, the earth split open, grain made to grow (80:24-27).
events.note: The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: When Arabia was green
events.what: Heavier rains turn Arabia into grassland with lakes and herds. Rock art at Jubbah shows the cattle. Then, slowly, the land dries again.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour will not come until the land of the Arabs returns to meadows and rivers.
events.note: The hadith is reported by Muslim. Arabia had several green phases; this one ended by about 4000 BCE.

events.title: Maize in Mexico
events.what: Farmers in southern Mexico breed a wild grass into maize. It will feed the Olmec, the Maya and the Aztecs.
events.tie: The Quran describes rain bringing out green shoots and 'grains arranged in layers' (6:99).
events.note: The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: Rice and millet in China
events.what: Villages along the Yellow and Yangtze rivers grow millet and rice. At Jiahu people also carve the oldest playable flutes.
events.tie: The Quran counts 'crops of different kinds of food' among Allah's gifts (6:141).
events.note: The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.

events.title: Eridu, the first city
events.what: A town grows around a temple at Eridu in southern Iraq. Sumerians later remember it as the first city, where kingship began before a great flood.
events.tie: Flood memories survive in Mesopotamia and far beyond; the Quran tells Nuh's flood as 'a sign for the worlds' (29:15).
events.note: The Quran gives no date for Adam or Nuh; this order follows scientific dating and is not a claim about when they lived.
